topics.title: Nets, Areas and Volumes of Solids
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Form nets of common solids. (u, s)
Identify common solids and their properties including faces, edges and vertices. (k)
Convert units from one form to another. (u)
Calculate surface areas of three-dimensional figures. (u, s)
Calculate the volume of cubes and cuboids. (u, s)

body.text: A net is a 2D shape that folds up to make a 3D solid. A cube's net is six identical squares arranged so they fold into a box; a cuboid's net is three pairs of matching rectangles. The surface area of a solid is the total area of all the faces in its net added together.

A cuboid measures 5 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm. It has three pairs of rectangular faces: two of 5x3, two of 5x4, and two of 3x4. Surface area = 2(5x3) + 2(5x4) + 2(3x4) = 2(15) + 2(20) + 2(12) = 30 + 40 + 24 = 94 cm^2.

The volume of a cuboid (and a cube, its special case) is length x width x height. The same cuboid (5 cm x 3 cm x 4 cm) has volume 5 x 3 x 4 = 60 cm^3. When converting units, remember 1 cm^3 = 1000 mm^3 and 1 m^3 = 1 000 000 cm^3, since each linear dimension scales by the conversion factor.
